dedupe_keys.name: whymap world wide hydrogeological maps and data bgr and unesco

description: The World-wide Hydrogeological Mapping and Assessment Programme, WHYMAP, was launched in 2000 by BGR and UNESCO to compile groundwater information from national, regional and global sources and publish it as maps, web map applications and services. The maps and data page lists the products with their years: Groundwater Resources of the World (2008), River and Groundwater Basins of the World (2012), Global Groundwater Vulnerability to Floods and Droughts (2015), World Karst Aquifer Map (2017), Groundwater Resources of Africa (2018), Groundwater Resources in the ECOWAS Region (2022) and the Mediterranean Karst Aquifer Map (2023), plus additional maps and a map viewer and service. The programme estimates world groundwater resources at 10.5 million cubic kilometres. BGR and UNESCO hold the copyright but allow use and reproduction without further permission if they are acknowledged; metadata documentation attached to each dataset gives the citation. Coverage: global to regional maps at small scale. Access: free downloads and a viewer. Caveats: the maps are coarse compilations of varying source quality and not for local aquifer design. They give the aquifer and basin context for water supply, irrigation and drought vulnerability simulations, and complement the IGRAC groundwater information system record already catalogued.
